---
name: cis-bounded-planning
description: Build, import feature specifications into, inspect, and validate dependency-aware CIS work plans from accepted impact findings. Use when impact review is complete and work must be bounded by complexity, objectives, dependencies, acceptance criteria, validation, and approval gates before implementation.
---

# CIS Bounded Planning

Apply the canonical code-quality standard's proportionate implementation policy before decomposing work. State accepted behavior and owner, exclusions, the simplest direct approach/supplied example, and the accepted need for any material deviation in existing task fields. Explicit later user decisions can supersede examples; an agent plan or tests cannot invent responsibilities. Challenge an unnecessary framework as a whole instead of making its parts medium-sized. Derive task and verification applicability from accepted positive behavior, explicit obligations and adopted policy, not metadata, negation or excluded examples. Preserve required shared/release obligations at their actual boundary without a fresh release campaign for every implementation story.

1. Run `cis impact analyse <change-id>` against the approved feature scope.
2. For a current explicitly approved CIS feature, run `cis plan derive <change-id> --file <repo-relative-spec.md>`. This atomically carries the existing authority through eligible deterministic impacts, any untouched proposal-acceptance placeholder, and the exact validated plan; do not request separate impact or plan approvals when it succeeds. Existing human-managed proposal criteria are preserved.
3. If derivation stops, surface only the reported low-confidence, deferred, truncated, conflicting, stale, or invalid exception. Use explicit `cis impact accept|reject|defer`, `cis plan import-spec`, and `cis plan approve` only as the fallback after the human resolves that exception. When no governed feature exists, use `cis plan build <change-id>`; it materializes real bounded task documents/catalogue links without requiring a feature pack. Identities follow retained impact bindings, including retirement/reactivation history, rather than sort positions. Unchanged rebuilds preserve entire authored contracts. A changed or missing input basis, ambiguous legacy owner or invalid/missing document requires targeted reconciliation before approval; never overwrite authored scope or recycle an old owner's identity to bypass that hold.
4. Run `cis plan show <change-id>` and open every linked `agent-tasks/WORK-NNN.md`; the plan table is only the dependency ledger, not the complete task contract. After re-import, inspect `agent-tasks/retired/`, archived catalog routes, and `plan-task-retired|reactivated` events; preserved evidence never grants renewed completion.
5. Verify each task has bounded required changes, exclusions, accepted graph evidence, dependencies and gates, acceptance checklists, targeted validation, a completion-evidence table, and explicit deferral/residual-risk handling. Generated `test-cases.md` and `test-cases.csv` retain stable derived planning identities; their existence does not independently require another task output or automation campaign. Where accepted requirements, explicit task outputs or adopted policy require catalogue traceability, check the stable manual cases and Markdown-recorded CSV hash, place each applicable `TC-*` ID in its automated test name, framework metadata or adjacent traceability annotation, and rerun the unchanged import to refresh `repository::path:line` mappings. `Pending` is allowed during planning; the required scoped cases must be `Automated` at final verification. Record executions in `verification.md`, not in the generated catalogue.
6. Classify every UI-bearing requirement, screen, wireframe task, design task, and frontend implementation task as exactly `public`, `customer`, or `backoffice`. Generate a matched wireframe -> design -> frontend chain for each affected type.
7. For every unauthenticated endpoint, require `PUBLIC-ENDPOINT-CACHE` obligations in Security, API contract, Backend, Observability, Verification, and Independent assurance: every response traverses a governed cache and the public route/controller/handler never directly accesses a database or repository, including on cache miss.
8. For UI-bearing scope, require validated wireframes -> design approval -> every downstream task; a separately owned coordination task may precede that chain when justified. Treat `wireframes.md` and `design.md` as canonical review records. By default `cis design approve` approves the exact wireframe digest and rendered design pack together; use standalone wireframe approval only when an early behavior-only checkpoint is intentionally requested. When design enters `ReadyForReview`, stop all non-review work until explicit approval.
9. Generate the smallest task set justified by independently owned outcomes, handoffs or approval boundaries. Keep acceptance, documentation, native verification, independent review and completion checks within implementation work unless a real separate deliverable warrants another task. Do not create coordination, documentation, verification, assurance or final-sweep tasks merely because those obligations exist. Preserve existing reviewed task identities, authored contracts, statuses and useful results on refresh. UI, migration, cross-repository and other genuinely separate outcomes may still have separate tasks. Product-specific search/projection belongs to an extension provider, not CIS core.
10. For volume-sensitive work, identify bytes, records, shape, concurrency and CPU/memory/time/storage limits before rollout. Record a representative end-to-end result separately from component and installation results using `workload-evidence.json` as documented in `cis plan validate`. Missing applicable evidence blocks completion of the work that owns that obligation, or its separately planned Final Delivery Sweep; inapplicability needs a concrete rationale. This does not authorize experiments or resource changes.
11. Confirm executable delivery leaves are at most medium. Retain high items as containers with bounded children. Assess breadth, interfaces, state/concurrency, coordination and uncertainty with a current scope basis and rationale; an unknown or stale assessment requires targeted planning before implementation. Reasoning strength remains independent of delivery size.
12. Preserve each logical task instance and exact dependency IDs across reload/reimport. A reusable category/type is not an instance identity; ambiguous legacy type references need targeted resolution. Carry category, type/version, outputs, criteria, negative criteria and actionable verification obligations into execution and completion. A check may cover several criteria; a criterion may require several checks. Adopted shared gates still apply. Run `cis plan validate <change-id>` and resolve every error. Use `cis plan task transition <change-id> <task-id> --status <state> --actor <identity> --reason <rationale>` for lifecycle changes. Completion requires resolved evidence and snapshots sanitized tool-usage counts/savings into the task and `verification.md`.
13. If planning reports an extension capability conflict, run `cis plan capability status`, present all candidates, and use `cis plan capability select` only after explicit human selection. Selection never migrates existing tasks; use `cis plan task migrate-type` with human reviewer and rationale for each compatible instance.
14. Run `cis plan approve <change-id> --reviewer <identity> --reason <rationale>` only when new plan authority is required and the user explicitly approves the exact validated issue pack. Never duplicate a successful `cis plan derive` approval.

Never forge or infer feature authority, approve a plan autonomously, hide advisory warnings, remove accepted scope to make validation pass, or treat a draft plan as implementation authority.
